title: Explicit Rate of Convergence O(log l / l) for Erdős #1014 k=3

problemStatement.plain: Prove an explicit quantitative rate bound for the convergence R(3,l+1)/R(3,l) → 1. While OQ-01 proved ε-δ convergence, this gives the concrete rate O(log l / l) with C = 2/c where c is the Kim-Shearer constant.
whyMatters: Strengthens OQ-01 convergence to a quantitative rate bound
Rate is sharp: recurrence forces O(l) increments, Kim-Shearer gives Θ(l²/log l) denominator
Universal rate O(log l / l) for all k ≥ 3 under conjectured asymptotics

proven: explicit_rate_k3: ∃ C > 0, ∃ L₀, ∀ l > L₀, |R(3,l+1)/R(3,l) - 1| ≤ C · log(l)/l
knownResults.goal: ACHIEVED: Explicit rate bound proved with C = 2/c

currentState.focus: Explicit rate bound O(log l / l) for k=3

knowledge.progressSummary: PROGRESS: Main results proved (rate_of_convergence_k3, log_over_l_faster_than_inv_log). 2 sorries remain in conditional_rate_general_k (Bernoulli bound + factor decomposition). Axioms from parent file (Ramsey definitions).
builtItems: Erdos1014OQ02.lean: explicit_rate_k3 — main theorem with quantitative rate
insights: Rate is sharp: recurrence gives O(l) increment, Kim-Shearer gives Θ(l²/log l), ratio is Θ(log l/l)
Key algebra: (l+1)·log l/(c·l²) ≤ 2l·log l/(c·l²) = (2/c)·log l/l for l ≥ 1
The O(log l/l) rate is UNIVERSAL for all k ≥ 3 under conjectured asymptotics: recurrence always gains one power of l in denominator vs increment
For general k: R(k,l+1)-R(k,l) ≤ R(k-1,l+1) ~ l^{k-2}/(log l)^{k-3} while R(k,l) ~ l^{k-1}/(log l)^{k-2}, ratio ~ log l/l
conditional_rate_general_k sorries: (1) Bernoulli-type bound on (1+1/l)^a · (log/log)^b product, (2) 3-factor decomposition combining asymptotics. Both are correct analysis but hard to formalize.
nextSteps: General k conditional rate theorem (requires power/log arithmetic)
